queries: Kalai Vempala 2024 calibrated language models must hallucinate

sources_considered.why: Original technical analysis identifies hallucination under idealized predictive learning and states the limits of that result.
Verifies the March 2024 version date and publication in STOC 2024.
The version public before the post analyzes general learning limits that do not depend on software bugs.
The current abstract reflects a February 2025 revision; the January 2024 version was used instead.

evidence_items.publisher: Kalai and Vempala; STOC 2024, author version on arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 1, Introduction, discussion of prediction versus generation
evidence_items.explanation: The analysis establishes a statistical source of hallucination for calibrated predictors of certain arbitrary facts, even with ideal factual training data. The result is independent of transformer architecture and permits mitigation, so it supports the ordinary structural-tendency reading rather than architectural inevitability.

The paper derives limitations from the inability to learn every computable ground-truth function, without assuming an implementation defect. Its broad formal definition does not establish an unavoidable error rate for any particular practical task.

unresolved_gaps: These results do not establish that transformer architecture itself uniquely causes hallucinations or that practical mitigation cannot succeed.
